offence_severity: rigorous imprisonment for life uls 396 IPC
physical_harm: death of one victim and grievous injuries to the other
number_of_offences: The appellant was prosecuted for 8 offences punishable under ss 395, 396 and 397 IPC. Out of the said 5 accused, two remained absconding; and two being juveniles, their case was separated. The trial court convicted the appellant under each of the three counts
financial_property_loss: Rs.4,000/- to 5,000/- cash as well as the ornaments worn by P.W.9 on her neck and hands
key_evidence_accepted: The conviction of the appellant for his involvement in the crime with four others falling u/ss 395, 396 and 397 IPC, as recorded by trial court and confirmed by High Court, does not call for any interference.
witness_credibility: P.W.9, the victim, was able to observe the conduct of the appellant and other accused so closely giving no scope for any doubt as to her unhesitant identification of the appellant at the time of trial.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 13/14.06.2004; Trial judgment: 09.05.2005; High Court decision: 25.04.2007; Supreme Court decision: 04.09.2012
legal_representation: Rajiv Nanda for the Appellant; Aprajita Sinha, Asha Gopalan Nair for the Respondent
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction confirmed; High Court: Conviction confirmed; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant, along with four others, committed dacoity resulting in the death of one victim and grievous injuries to another. They emphasized the victim's testimony identifying the appellant as one of the assailants, medical evidence of the victim's injuries, and the recovery of stolen items from the appellant.
defence_argument: The defence contended that the offence of dacoity was not made out as the basic ingredient of five persons committing robbery and murder was not established. They also argued that no recoveries of stolen articles were made and that the identification of the appellant without a proper test identification parade could not form the basis of his conviction.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that participation in an offence with a group of five or more persons indulging in robbery and committing murder or causing grievous hurt with deadly weapons is sufficient for conviction under Sections 395, 396, and 397 of the IPC.
precedent_relied_upon: Dana Yadav alias Oahu and others v. State of Bihar (2002) 7 SCC 295, Simon and others v. State of Karnataka (2004) 2 SCC 694, Daya Singh v. State of Haryana (2001) 1 SCR 1115, and Suraj Pal v. State of Haryana (1995) 2 SCC 64
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the appellant's involvement in the crime with four others, resulting in the death of one victim and grievous injuries to another, was established beyond doubt by the evidence, including the victim's testimony and recovery of stolen items.
